speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Our current capabilities in managing communicable diseases reside in several entities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, the Ministry of Health (MOH) sets policy, the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID) administers the public health control measures as part of the national programmes and the Heath Promotion Board (HPB) does public education.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, how can Singaporeans be assured that the CDA will achieve results greater than the sum of its parts?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: By consolidating critical public health functions from three key institutions under one agency, we aim for efficiency and effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will this restructuring translate into tangible public health benefits?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Each of the existing entities hold deep expertise in areas like policy development, surveillance and operational responses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What mechanisms will ensure that the strengths of these institutions are fully leveraged under the CDA's umbrella?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The CDA’s role as a coordinating authority is critical.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: On-the-ground work will continue to involve multiple players, including public institutions and private contractors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Ministry ensure that CDA has the authority, resources and the tools to harmonise these efforts?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, I have queries about the transfer of employees to CDA.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A disruption in essential health services during this transition could have severe repercussions, especially if a disease outbreak occurs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What measures are in place to retrain and upskill employees for the broader mandates of CDA?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Ensuring that the workforce is equipped with new skills will be vital for tackling emerging and complex diseases.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The preservation of institutional knowledge is equally important.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Employees who have led critical public health initiatives, such as vaccination drives, carry invaluable experience.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will their expertise be retained and their morale maintained during this transition?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Additionally, how will union representation be addressed as employees move from the civil service to a statutory board?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What safeguards are in place for those who may decline the transfer?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the National Trades Union Congress be involved?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, public health is not the sole responsibility of a single agency.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could we see the formation of joint task forces or integrated data systems to enhance early detection and coordinated responses?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clear public communication is also critical during outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be a single, unified messaging platform to ensure that Singaporeans receive accurate and timely information without confusion?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Fourth, Mr Speaker, Sir, infectious diseases know no borders.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We know from SARS and, most recently, COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am glad to hear from the Minister of State just now that CDA will play an active role in global health initiatives to protect Singaporeans from external threats.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the CDA work with international organisations, like the WHO, to share insights and access critical information?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will it participate in joint surveillance systems to identify emerging threats directly and early?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Beyond immediate measures, will CDA advocate for stronger international regulations and lead global efforts in pandemic preparedness, including vaccine research and diagnostics?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Resilience in public health is not just desirable, it is essential.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The establishment of the CDA offers an opportunity to elevate Singapore’s public health defences.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, we must ensure it delivers on its promise.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The CDA must unite and strengthen public health functions to benefit Singaporeans, ensure a smooth and morale-boosting transition for employees, retaining their expertise, collaborate effectively with agencies, like NEA, to address multi-dimensional health challenges and engage globally to stay ahead of emerging threats.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The current health situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo underscores the urgency of proactive measures.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Stricter health screenings and quarantine protocols for travelers from Africa or transit hubs in the Middle East are critical in shielding Singapore from potential risks.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Over the past week, an outbreak of HMPV in China and Malaysia have also raised alarms globally.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: CDA must act with foresight, anticipate risks, coordinate responses and build trust with Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This agency should not merely serve as a safety net, but as a proactive force that protects lives and inspires confidence.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Let us seize this moment to set a new standard in public health.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We will, nevertheless, offer three additional suggestions on the scope and objectives of the new institution as it commences its service to Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: First, we believe that the emergency preparedness and response mandate of CDA has to be sufficiently broad.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This means that the institution should not only be focused on the most stereotypical public health emergencies, which have to do with disease outbreaks like epidemics and pandemics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The CDA should also regard disaster management as a key part of its scenario planning parameters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While Singapore, thankfully, rarely encounters the standard range of natural disasters, such as earthquakes, tsunamis or wildfires, flooding remains common in spite of advances in our water management infrastructure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While communicable waterborne diseases, such as cholera, are, thankfully, very rare in modern Singapore, cases do sporadically arise as they did in 2009.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: By a similar token, man-made disasters, such as chemical or, perhaps in the future, radiological incidents, would also potentially have associated disease transmission risks and have to be planned for.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Perhaps more crucially, CDA should also consider the implications of bioterrorist threats, such as smallpox or engineered virus strains.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While the Ministry of Defence or the Ministry of Home Affairs would undoubtedly be tasked with how best to counter such attacks, the management of the aftermath of a bioweapons outbreak would logically fall under the scope of the new CDA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But CDA should not confine its mandate to emergencies alone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Many communicable diseases are ongoing and, possibly, seasonal, such as dengue or influenza.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Their routine nature should, however, not diminish their risks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This would mean enfolding seemingly mundane tasks, like the provision of educational and informational advisories on communicable disease prevention, into the priorities for the new agency.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: CDA should be leading public informational campaigns ranging from things that seem mundane like annual flu shots to prevention strategies for HIV.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Indeed, it is sometimes the non-clinical aspects of such diseases – ensuring the undisrupted supply chain of masks and other critical medical supplies or regulating appropriate safeguards for close quarter living spaces, which was an acknowledged oversight in our COVID-19 response – that may be the most critical.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We understand, of course, that many of these roles currently fall to different agencies and Ministries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Dengue and Zika, for example, are overseen by NEA; while the various strains of influenza are currently monitored directly by MOH.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry will almost inevitably be involved in supply chain matters and foreign worker dormitories currently fall under the purview of the Ministry of Manpower.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Research funding for vaccine research would be naturally administered by the National Research Foundation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Perhaps the Minister of State would be willing to explain how the different roles will be re-allocated going forward if, indeed, the new CDA will have frontline oversight over all communicable diseases.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And this, in turn, will mean the need to establish constant channels of communication and coordination, insofar as infectious diseases are concerned.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The new CDA must be proactive in this process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Most evidently, this would be within Singapore, both between Government bodies, but also with allied institutions, such as clinics and hospitals or university research centres.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It would also entail coordinating the process of international knowledge and information exchange, an important objective that the Government itself acknowledges and Minister of State Rahayu just alluded to, so that we do not necessarily re-invent the wheel or go down unproductive paths in our scientific and policy decisions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: One common complaint during the COVID-19 pandemic was how information and guidance from MOH seemed to change by the week and releases were often confusing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While we appreciate that the management of an ever-evolving disease is necessarily dynamic, it should not preclude the deployment of simple and reliable communication strategies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: With recent lapses in interagency communication surrounding the failed Allianz-Income deal, multiple MRT service disruptions and the most recent Bizfile NRIC leak, it behooves us to ensure that similar breakdowns do not recur in times of crisis when we can least afford it.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The Bill represents a significant step in strengthening our nation's capabilities to prevent, manage and control infectious diseases.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Its importance is underscored by the growing complexity of global health challenges as we saw during the COVID-19 pandemic and the ongoing need to combat diseases, like dengue and influenza.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: During COVID-19, for instance, the rapid spread of the virus and the pressure on our healthcare system highlighted the critical need for a robust, centralised agency to manage such crises effectively.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: While I fully support the intent behind this Bill, I would like to raise some questions and seek clarification on key provisions.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: First, I would like to address the potential impact of this transition on our existing public health services.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The transfer of functions from MOH and HPB to CDA is a significant organisational shift.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Can the Ministry share a detailed transition plan to mitigate any disruptions or any risks of disruptions?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: These services are the backbone of our public health framework and any gaps, even temporary ones, could have severe implications for our citizens' health and well-being.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The Bill outlines broad powers for CDA, including managing significant resources and overseeing critical public health functions.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Transparency will be essential for maintaining public health in this new agency.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Public trust in CDA is paramount, especially when it is new and these measures will go a long way to ensure accountability and trust.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: CDA's broad mandate raises important questions about the prioritisation of its resources.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Balancing immediate needs with long-term growth is critical.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Could the Ministry provide an outline of its initial funding allocations and provide for CDA to align public expectations with operational realities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Effective resource management will be critical to the success of this agency and clarity in this regard will help in aligning public expectations with operational realities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I also wish to highlight the importance of protecting the welfare of employees who will be transferred from MOH and HPB to CDA.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Our healthcare workers have been instrumental in safeguarding our nation's health, especially during the pandemic.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Will there be a structured consultation process to address employees' concerns during this transition?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: These employees are the foundation of CDA's operations and their welfare should remain a top priority to ensure a smooth transition and continued excellence in public health services.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The Bill empowers CDA to represent Singapore internationally on matters related to infectious diseases.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This international engagement is crucial for fostering global partnerships and ensuring our policies are aligned with best practices worldwide.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: During the pandemic, a multi-agency task force was set up to coordinate responses across various sectors.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: How will CDA's international engagement impact or complement such multi-agency efforts?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: To avoid overlap or misalignment with existing strategies, could the Ministry clarify how CDA's international engagements will complement ongoing work by MOH and other agencies?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Could the Ministry also share the specific coordination mechanisms that will be established to ensure streamlined communication and unified representation on the global stage?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Such protocols will enhance our credibility and effectiveness in global health matters.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The establishment of CDA offers an opportunity to not only strengthen our infectious diseases management capabilities but also reaffirm our commitment to transparency, accountability and the welfare of those who will serve in this critical agency.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Let us take a moment to acknowledge the dedication of our healthcare workers who have tirelessly protected our nation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Their resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic exemplifies the spirit we aim to preserve and enhance with CDA.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Notwithstanding the clarifications raised, I support the Bill.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the mechanisms to ensure that CDA will be able to leverage the strengths of MOH, HPB and NCID fully, given that each of these entities already hold deep expertise in various aspects of public health.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will create an ecosystem where public health practitioners can share knowledge and solve problems together.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will also be strengthening both our capabilities and capacities for communicable disease prevention, control and response.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Under CDA, these talented professionals will have greater opportunities to grow, learn from one another and raise standards in public health practice.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As Dr Wan Rizal rightly pointed out, critical public health functions must continue seamlessly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Since the Minister for Health's announcement of CDA's formation in March 2023, we have ensured a smooth transition, with our public health operations remaining robust and effective throughout this period of change.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have also worked on refining our work processes to enhance critical public health functions and activities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Next, I will move on to other questions posed by Members.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the measures in place to protect and develop staff.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have been conducting regular engagement sessions with staff and unions to provide information and seek feedback.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Throughout this transition, we have consulted with the respective organisations and the Public Service Division.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The new CDA scheme is designed to support the professional growth, career progression and development of CDA's officers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To grow expertise, CDA will provide structured learning opportunities to equip officers with the relevant competencies to perform their jobs effectively.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: CDA officers will also be given opportunities to rotate to other roles and functions within CDA, across the wider healthcare or public service family, and even obtain international exposure.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim also asked about CDA's role in multi-agency coordination.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As part of the transition, we have ensured that CDA's work aligns with national policies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: CDA will continue to work closely with MOH and other public agencies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For instance, today we work closely with NEA to mitigate the impact of vector-borne diseases like dengue fever, with the Singapore Food Agency on food safety and with the National Parks Board on diseases that may affect both animals and humans.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These collaborations are part of a multi-agency cooperation framework termed "One Health".

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: CDA will continue to work with the One Health agencies as part of a multi-sectoral, integrated approach to prevent, detect and respond to new and emerging public health threats.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Our preparedness and response plans for "Disease X", as asked by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, also includes tapping on the whole-of-Government agencies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This recognises the wide impact of outbreaks and pandemics, and the need for a multi-pronged effort.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Working with other Ministries and agencies is not just during a crisis, but also during non-crisis periods.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is part of our efforts to enhance Singapore's preparedness and readiness for pandemics, and also for the control of endemic diseases.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To enhance communication and coordination, CDA will build upon existing platforms and strengthen information exchanges with all stakeholders, including timely sharing of important information with the public.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Both Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Yip Hon Weng have asked about CDA's role in the area of international engagement, including working with organisations, such as WHO to advance our public health interests.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As diseases know no borders, CDA will represent Singapore on infectious diseases at relevant fora to establish strategic collaborations with our bilateral and multilateral counterparts, and to bolster global disease preparedness and response.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: CDA will also contribute actively to international scientific and surveillance networks to facilitate the exchange of disease information and sharing of expertise.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This will allow Singapore to detect and understand novel pathogens faster, which can buy us time to respond.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Upon establishment, CDA will also be a national member of the International Association of National Public Health Institutes to closely engage and collaborate with other national public health institutes worldwide.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's point about expanding to disaster management, the CDA's aims is to focus on communicable diseases, as its expertise is in this area.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For natural or man-made disasters, MOH and other Ministries already have the capabilities to respond to them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: CDA will work together with these Ministries and agencies on the communicable disease issues that will arise.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Given CDA's mandate for end-to-end disease prevention, preparation, detection and management, it will need sufficient support for its manpower and resources to achieve its objectives.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: CDA will also comply with the financial governance requirements under Public Sector (Governance) Act 2018.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Any Members have clarifications for the Minister of State?
